references.text: In this verse they again attempt to seize Jesus, but no one lays hands on him because his hour has not yet come, mirroring the situation in John 7:44 where fear of the crowd prevents his arrest.
Here the Jews try once more to seize Jesus, but he escapes their grasp, a repetition of the pattern in John 7:44 where no one is able to lay hands on him.
This is the final moment when Jesus allows himself to be seized; the soldiers lay hands on him, marking the end of the period during which no one could arrest him, as described in John 7:44.

Pilate says that they may take and crucify him themselves, but the Jews reply that they are not permitted to put anyone to death, underscoring that it was divine protection that prevented his arrest earlier, just as in John 7:44.
